title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's controls, credit billing and feature behaviour are supported by Microsoft documentation, and its availability statements match the supplied roadmap record. Correct the roadmap source link: it points to a different item.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 562222 has status Launched.
claims.quote: "id": 562222; "status": "Launched"; "roadmapUrl": "https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?id=562222"

claims.claim: The agent node hands a workflow step to an agent that reasons, calls tools and reads knowledge before returning a result.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The agent response becomes dynamic content for subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: Makers open Workflows, open or create a workflow, use Build for an existing workflow, and select Agent on the Add panel.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to **Workflows** and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. ... Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab. ... Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel.

claims.claim: An existing agent is selected from a list of published agents.
claims.quote: **An existing agent**: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: An existing agent uses its already configured instructions, tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow creates an inline agent scoped to that workflow.
claims.quote: **New agent for this workflow**: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape are configured in the node and travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Makers can optionally attach Model Context Protocol servers as tools.
claims.quote: Give the node an instruction, optionally attach tools and knowledge, and you're done. ... **Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers**: Prebuilt servers that expose a curated set of capabilities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Any Power Platform connector action can be attached as a tool.
claims.quote: **Connectors**: Any Power Platform connector action.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent decides at runtime which attached tools to call, their order and their arguments.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Public websites can ground the inline agent's responses.
claims.quote: **Public websites**: Index one or more public URLs so the agent can cite content from those sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: SharePoint can ground the inline agent's responses.
claims.quote: **SharePoint**: Connect to a SharePoint site, library, or specific document so the agent can answer from internal content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Work IQ setting lets the agent use the running user's recent mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive and SharePoint context.
claims.quote: Turn on **Work IQ** to let the agent use the running user's recent work activity, including mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive, and SharePoint context, to ground its responses.

claims.claim: Request human assistance when unsure is a maker setting reached through Workflows > workflow > Build > Add panel > Agent.
claims.quote: Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab. ... Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel. ... Turn on **Request human assistance when unsure** to let the agent escalate when it isn't confident enough to act on its own.

claims.claim: Human assistance emails the connection owner for input.
claims.quote: The agent emails the connection owner for input and waits for a reply before continuing.

claims.claim: Human assistance waits for a reply before continuing.
claims.quote: The agent emails the connection owner for input and waits for a reply before continuing.

claims.claim: Without tools, the agent can only read and reason.
claims.quote: Without tools, the agent can only read and reason.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Attached tools let the agent act, including sending messages and invoking APIs.
claims.quote: Tools give the agent the ability to *do* actions such as send a message, query a record, run a search, or call an API.

claims.claim: Structured output exposes individual fields for downstream actions.
claims.quote: When you pick a structured output, each field becomes its own dynamic-content token that downstream actions can reference directly.

claims.claim: Evaluations are only available for new agents created in workflows.
claims.quote: Evaluations are only available for new agents created in workflows.

claims.claim: Up to 20 evaluations can run per agent node per day.
claims.quote: You can run up to 20 evaluations per agent node per day.

claims.claim: New workflow runs are blocked when environment prepaid capacity is fully consumed until capacity is available.
claims.quote: Once you fully consume your environment's prepaid Copilot Studio capacity, new workflow runs are blocked until capacity is available.

claims.claim: Running workflows complete normally when prepaid capacity is exhausted.
claims.quote: Running workflows complete normally.

claims.claim: Workflows otherwise follow a defined sequence of actions and rule-based branches.
claims.quote: Workflows follow a defined sequence of actions and rule-based branches, making process execution predictable. Results can vary when actions use AI or retrieve changing data.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Using, building, testing and evaluating the agent node can consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption, with workflow and agent usage measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Workflows run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user are covered by Microsoft 365 Copilot; other workflow cases are billed.
claims.quote: | Workflows | Yes, when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user | Billed in all other cases. |

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges Copilot Credits for LLM tokens.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges Copilot Credits for tools, including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness itself consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Billing for the Microsoft Copilot harness starts when building starts.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Testing and evaluating Microsoft Copilot harness agents consume credits.
claims.quote: Experiences such as creating an automated solution with natural language, previewing and testing an agent, and generating and creating agent evaluations all consume credits.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A rate specific to the agent node is not published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" "credits" rate pricing. Read agent-node-workflow, agents-experience/billing-credit-overview and manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness; searched requirements-messages-management excerpts, which concern the standard harness. No node-specific rate found.

claims.claim: Cost is variable because usage is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The number of Copilot Credits these experiences consume depends on how they are designed, how often they run, and the features they use.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment capacity controls govern all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment, including agents, workflows and prompts.
claims.quote: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment, not only agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness. Review standard-harness agents, Microsoft Copilot harness agents, agent flows, workflows, prompts, and other credit-consuming features

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Tenant draw is configured in Power Platform admin center through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**. ... Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**. ... Select **Manage Copilot Credits**. ... Select the environment. ... Under **Capacity overages**, clear **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request uses allocation.quantity inside allocatedEntitlements to set allocated credits.
claims.quote: allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages" allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 }

claims.claim: MCSMessages is the entitlement ID representing Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID `MCSMessages`

claims.claim: An enforcementRules entry with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false disables tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: enforcementRules = @( # Disable TenantPool so the environment is capped at its allocation. # Set enabled = $true to let the environment draw from tenant capacity. @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.claim: Managing capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role with licensing and capacity permissions.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Eligible environments with no allocation configuration have tenant-capacity draw selected by default.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; controls[0]
claims.claim: Clearing tenant draw prevents consuming unallocated tenant prepaid capacity after the environment allocation runs out.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation.

claims.claim: Clearing tenant draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify administrators but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Without an enabled overage source, an environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: An environment group rule governing tenant draw makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override an environment group's tenant-draw rule.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio shows Agent flow actions used by each workflow.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center > **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**, review the **Agent flow actions** used by each workflow.

claims.claim: The printed GET environment resources request with fromDate, toDate and API version 2024-10-01 is documented.
claims.quote: GET https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/entitlements/{entitlementId}/environments/{environmentId}/resources?fromDate={fromDate}&toDate={toDate}&api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: The environment resources API is deprecated.
claims.quote: Get environment resource entitlement snapshots for an entitlement (deprecated).

claims.claim: The environment resources API returns environment resource entitlement consumption snapshots.
claims.quote: Get environment resource entitlement snapshots for an entitlement (deprecated). ... consumed | number (double) | The consumed value.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column.
claims.quote: The **Credit usage (last 30 days)** column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio has centralised Work IQ MCP governance in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: **Centralized governance**: Admins manage Work IQ MCP in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Allowing or disallowing tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not yet be available in every region.
claims.quote: The ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not be available in your region yet.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP has a tenant-level policy layer that evaluates each MCP tool request.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. ... Policy layer | Applies tenant governance rules to each MCP tool request

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy when available.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select **Agents** > **Tools**. ... In the tools registry, select **Work IQ MCP**. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the **Policy** tab when it's available.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support certified connectors.
claims.quote: **Certified connectors** | Supported | First-party and certified third-party connectors. Full allow/block at the connector and action level.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support MCP server governance.
claims.quote: Advanced connector policies support visibility and management of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom and HTTP connectors are not yet supported by Advanced Connector Policies.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Classic data policies are the documented governance route for custom and HTTP connectors.
claims.quote: For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic data policies.

claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policy design-time enforcement is rolling out to Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order: 1. **Power Automate maker portal** ... 2. **Copilot Studio**

claims.claim: Until design-time enforcement is available, Advanced Connector Policies enforce only at runtime for the workload.
claims.quote: Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.where: controls[3]; summary; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no tenant switch dedicated to disabling the agent node itself or its node-specific settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" disable tenant admin switch. Read agent-node-workflow, flows-overview, manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness, admin-data-loss-prevention and Work IQ governance. Results document broader controls, not a dedicated agent-node switch.

claims.claim: The node is user-opt-in because a maker chooses to add it in the designer and no dedicated admin enablement switch is documented.
claims.quote: Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel. The configuration panel opens for the agent node.

claims.claim: An API for Request human assistance when unsure is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Request human assistance when unsure" API administrator policy. Read agent-node-workflow and search results. The feature is documented as a maker toggle; no matching API operation was returned.

claims.claim: No central setting is documented for Request human assistance when unsure.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Request human assistance when unsure" API administrator policy. Read agent-node-workflow and search results; no central enforcement setting was documented for this toggle.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The agent node page does not specify whose credentials its connector actions use.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" connector credentials identity preview. Read agent-node-workflow in full. General connector results describe user and maker connections, but the node page does not specify its connector execution identity.

claims.claim: The agent node Learn page does not identify which part of the feature remains in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" connector credentials identity preview. Read agent-node-workflow in full, including Known limitations and FAQs; it does not assign parts of the node to Preview versus General Availability.
